comparison.a: Strong O2 plugin architecture with detailed decisions and acceptance tests for MUST requirements, plus explicit determinism and security-default considerations. Milestones are comprehensive but less directly committed to several SHOULD items (e.g., GFM/exclusions) as concrete deliverables.
comparison.b: Clearer phased milestone plan (foundation then thin-slice plugins) with explicit exit criteria and inclusion of exclusions, GFM, and performance validation as concrete deliverables. Security governance is stronger/more explicit (pinning, sandboxing, reviews), though sandbox feasibility may depend on implementation stack.

evidence.note: A includes explicit determinism + security validation deliverables and exit criteria.
evidence.quote: Deterministic build check: repeated builds of the same input produce identical outputs

evidence.note: A sets realistic default trust model and safe rendering defaults for XSS/template risks.
evidence.quote: Default to a safe rendering mode: disallow or sanitize raw HTML in Markdown

evidence.note: B front-loads plugin API/engine/context with HITL approval before feature plugins.
evidence.quote: HITL review of plugin API contract completed and approved by Tech Lead.

evidence.note: B makes R20/R21 concrete deliverables with cross-browser validation in the same phase.
evidence.quote: File/directory exclusion support via config or CLI (R20).

payload.notes: B2B is more closure-ready due to clearer phased execution with explicit exit criteria and more concrete coverage of key SHOULD items (exclusions, GFM, performance). Main caveat is that proposed sandboxing for user-provided plugins/templates may be non-trivial depending on chosen language/runtime.
